instruction: You are an advanced AI model specialized in solving Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC) tasks.
input:
Each task will demonstrate a transformation from an input grid to an output grid. At the end, you will receive a new input grid. Your task is to determine its corresponding output grid. Your goal is to analyze a given set of input-output grids and deduce the underlying pattern or rule that transforms the input into the output. You are asked to provide an abstraction, filter, binding, and transformation that is applied to an input grid to correctly transfer it to the output grid.

Abstraction:
Graph abstraction allows us to search for a solution at a macroscopic level. In other words, we are modifying groups of pixels at once, instead of modifying each individual pixel separately.

Possible abstractions to choose from:
ccg: Creates a graph where each node represents a group of adjacent pixels of the same color.
ccgbr: Similar to ccg, but nodes identified as background (most common color and includes a corner) are removed.
ccgbr2: Similar to ccgbr, but background nodes also include those touching any edge of the image.
nbvcg: Creates a graph where each node is a group of vertically adjacent pixels of the same color, excluding background color.
nbhcg: Creates a graph where each node is a group of horizontally adjacent pixels of the same color, excluding background color.
nbccg: Similar to ccg, but excludes black pixels (color = 0).
lrg: Creates a graph where each node is a rectangle of adjacent pixels of the same color, identified from largest to smallest, excluding black pixels.
mcccg: Creates a graph where each node represents a group of adjacent pixels of any non-background color.
na: Creates a graph with the entire grid as one multi-color node.

Filters:
Filters are used to select specific nodes in the graph based on certain criteria.

Possible filters to choose from:
filter_by_color: Returns true if a node has a given color. Optionally, exclude nodes with the given color.
filter_by_size: Returns true if a node has a size equal to a given size. Optionally, exclude nodes of the given size.
filter_by_degree: Returns true if a node has a degree equal to a given degree. Optionally, exclude nodes of the given degree.
filter_by_neighbor_size: Returns true if a node has a neighbor of a given size. Optionally, exclude nodes with neighbors of the given size.
filter_by_neighbor_color: Returns true if a node has a neighbor of a given color. Optionally, exclude nodes with neighbors of the given color.
filter_by_neighbor_degree: Returns true if a node has a neighbor of a given degree. Optionally, exclude nodes with neighbors of the given degree.

When specifying a filter, also provide its parameters in a dictionary format like this:
{filter: filter_by_size, filter_params: {size: 2, exclude: False}}

Transformations:
Transformations are actions that change the properties or position of nodes.

Possible transformations to choose from:
update_color: Updates the color of a node to a given color. Parameters: {color}
move_node: Moves a node by 1 pixel in a specified direction. Parameters: {direction}
extend_node: Extends a node in a given direction, optionally allowing overlap with other nodes. Parameters: {direction, overlap}
move_node_max: Moves a node in a specified direction until it hits another node or the edge of the image. Parameters: {direction}
rotate_node: Rotates a node around its center point in a specified rotational direction. Parameters: {rotation_dir}
add_border: Adds a border with a specified color around a node. Parameters: {border_color}
fill_rectangle: Fills the rectangle containing a node with a specified color, optionally allowing overlap with other nodes. Parameters: {fill_color, overlap}
hollow_rectangle: Hollows the rectangle containing a node with a specified color. Parameters: {fill_color}
mirror: Mirrors a node with respect to a specified axis. Parameters: {mirror_axis}
flip: Flips a node in a specified direction (horizontal, vertical, diagonal left/right). Parameters: {mirror_direction}
remove_node: Removes a node from the graph.
insert: Inserts a pattern at a specified location relative to a given node and point. Parameters: {object_id, point, relative_pos}

Parameter Bindings:
Parameter bindings are used to dynamically select parameters for filters or transformations based on the properties of nodes.

Possible parameter bindings to choose from:
param_bind_neighbor_by_size: Returns a neighbor of a node that satisfies a given size filter.
param_bind_neighbor_by_color: Returns a neighbor of a node that satisfies a given color filter.
param_bind_node_by_shape: Returns any node in the graph with the same shape as a given node.
param_bind_node_by_size: Returns any node in the graph that satisfies a given size filter.
param_bind_neighbor_by_degree: Returns a neighbor of a node that satisfies a given degree filter.
